children: Shares of Biocon Ltd. declined on Monday, October 26, even as the company said it has secured market entry of Yesintek, a proposed biosimilar to Stelara, in additional global markets.

The company, in an exchange filing, said it has inked a licence agreement with Janssen Sciences Ireland clearing the way for the commercialization of Yesintek, its proposed biosimilar to Stelara, in Australia, Brazil, China, Hong Kong, Mexico, Israel, New Zealand, Kazakhstan and South Korea with immediate effect.
This builds on Biocon's previous agreements with Janssen that secured market entry dates for Yestinek in the US and in Europe, Canada, UK and Japan.

Biocon said these additional market entries for the biosimilar will allow the company to offer an affordable and effective treatment option for patients impacted by autoimmune diseases in these markets.

It said Yesintek is a human interleukin-12 and -12 antagonist that disrupts IL-12 and IL-23 mediated signaling in immune mediated diseases and has been approved for the treatment of Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis.
Stelara had global sales of $6.08 billion last year, Biocon reported, citing a Johnson & Johnson's 2025 sales report.
Biocon shares were down 0.3% at ₹322.4 apiece at 9.24 am. The stock has fallen 13.7% in the past month and is down 16.6% this year, so far.

title: Biocon gets additional global market entry for Yesintek to treat autoimmune diseases
